script: This NBA player had almost no chance of ever going pro, but somehow he still made it. In 2010, Duncan Robinson was only 5'7" as a high school freshman, barely got minutes, had no AAU experience, and came from a tiny New Hampshire town with around 1,000 people. By the time he finished high school, not one Division 1 school offered him a scholarship, and his only offer came from a Division 2 program. So instead, he went to Williams College, a Division 3 school with no athletic scholarships and basically no clear road to the NBA. But once he got there, everything changed. As a freshman, Robinson averaged 17 points while shooting 45% from three, carried Williams to the national championship game, and earned All-American honors. That's when Division 1 programs finally started paying attention, and he ended up transferring to Michigan as a walk-on with no promise that he would even play. But Robinson proved he belonged. In three seasons, he helped Michigan win two Big Ten titles and reach the 2018 national championship game against Villanova. Even after all that, every NBA team passed on him in the draft. So he signed a two-way deal with the Miami Heat for way less money than drafted rookies were making. But then his career exploded. In only his second season, Robinson broke Miami's franchise record with 270 three-pointers, started in the NBA Finals, and later became the fastest player ever to hit 1,000 career threes. Then in 2021, he signed a five-year, $90 million contract, the biggest deal ever for an undrafted player. He went from Division 3 with no obvious path to the league to making NBA history.
